title: Golden Gate Assembly Protocol for NEB Golden Gate Assembly Mix
author: Alba Balletbó
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7kfhktn
materials: For each assembly, thaw a 50 µL tube of NEB 10-beta competent E. coli cells on ice for 5–10 minutes.
Add 950 µL of room temperature NEB 10-beta/Stable Outgrowth Medium. Incubate at 37ºC for 60 minutes, shaking vigorously (250 rpm) or using a rotation device.

steps.title: Prepare 25 µL assembly reaction
steps.instruction: Set up each Golden Gate assembly reaction to a total volume of 25 µL as instructed, then mix gently by pipetting up and down four times and briefly microcentrifuge for 1 second to collect the mixture at the bottom of the tube.

steps.title: Run thermocycler program
steps.instruction: Transfer the assembled reaction to a thermocycler and run the following program: 5 min at 37 °C → 5 min at 16 °C, repeat for 30 cycles, then 5 min at 60 °C. If the reaction is left overnight, add a 4 °C terminal hold and repeat the final 5‑minute 60 °C step the next day before transformation.

steps.title: Add assembly to cells
steps.instruction: Add 2 µL of the completed assembly reaction to the competent cells, then gently mix by flicking the tube 4–5 times.

steps.title: Warm selective agar plates
steps.instruction: Warm LB agar plates containing chloramphenicol (for pGGA) at 37 °C for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Mix cells and plate outgrowth
steps.instruction: Mix the cells thoroughly by flicking the tube and inverting, then spread 100 µL of the outgrowth onto each warmed agar plate.

steps.title: Incubate plates
steps.instruction: Incubate the plates overnight at 37 °C, or for 24 hours at 30 °C, or for 48 hours at 25 °C, depending on desired colony development.
